text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- Ministries should not be split between two parties in the next government, says Finance Minister and Conservative Party Chairman Sauli Niinisto who now shares his ministry with social democrat Arja Alho.
- Parliament officials to re-examine nearby buildings as an alternative to new building.
- Parliament sets age limits and academic requirements for MP's assistants after some appointed their under-age children and retired parents to the job.
- Finnish entrepreneurs are confident of growing export markets in Russia and four out of five in survey expect a rise in exports to the east this year.
- Former KOP board member Pentti Rissanen wins case over his dismissal in a court of appeal, which ordered Merita to pay him two million markka.

- A rise in real earnings would hinder employment and the next round of pay talks should pay special attention to inflation forecasts, says The Goverment Institute of Economic Research (VATT) economist Pasi Holm.
- The European Commission will soon rule on Kesko's plan to sell parts of Tuko, says Kesko trustee Hannu Vanska at Arthur Andersen.
- The Finnish post will get a competitor next autumn when private firm Jantor's subsidiary Suoramainonta starts mail deliveries in the Helsinki area.
- Engineering group Rauma is not interested in rival Partek's forest machinery unit and has no plans to buy it, says Rauma CEO Heikki Hakala.

- Ministry of trade and industry pondering how to limit adverse effects of electricity market liberalisation: official says some acquisitions should have been stopped earlier to prevent vertical integration from going too far.

- Abolition of so-called transitional reserves will hit thousands of small companies which may be unable to turn the funds into investment with a rising tax burden as a result, entrepreneurs' lobby says.

- Nokia has in three years taken a clear lead over its rivals in South Africa and has a 40 percent stake of the mobile phone market, says Michael Myers, managing director of RF group which sells Nokia handsets in the country.
- Daily goods suppliers must pay so-called marketing support to wholesale and retail groups to make it to the shelves in Finland, says Tuko's ex-CEO Uolevi Manninen in a new book.
